title: How can one known product give three answers?
description: From the fact that forty five times twelve is five hundred forty, the board finds four point five times one point two, zero point four five times twelve and fifty four divided by one point two. Keeko's doubt is that four point five times one point two is fifty four.
teaching_notes: One idea: the digits of a product come from the known fact, and the total number of decimal places in the two numbers tells where the decimal point goes; for a division, multiply both numbers by ten or a hundred to match the fact. Ask the class whether four point five times one point two should be near five or near fifty before any work is shown. Watch for students who count the decimal places of only one number.

video_script.why: The child knows the rule for counting decimal places in a product but has not used one known fact to answer several questions.
video_script.substitution: The digits come from the fact, the decimal places of the two numbers tell where the point goes, and a divisor is made whole by multiplying both numbers by ten.
video_script.anchor: The fact 45 × 12 = 540 written on a card at the top of the board
video_script.wrong_move: counts only one decimal place, so 540 becomes 54.0 and the product is ten times too big
video_script.payoff_line: Four point five times one point two is five point four

final_answer.spoken: five point four, five point four and forty five

maths_rules: estimates: 4.5 x 1.2 is near 5 x 1 = 5; 0.45 x 12 is near 0.5 x 12 = 6
video_script.design: The fact card stays on the board all video. The working band builds the two products from the digits 540 with two decimal places, then the division by scaling, then an estimate. Keeko's doubt shows 540 with one place crossed out against the estimate near five.
open_questions: The book text has no solved example with the fact 45 times 12; the video follows the worklist example and the book's rules for decimal places and for a decimal divisor.

<bookmark mark='count'/>Zero point four five has two decimal places, and twelve has none. The product has two decimal places.

narration: <bookmark mark='est1'/>Step four, estimate to check. Four point five is near five, and one point two is near one. The product is near five.
<bookmark mark='est2'/>Zero point four five is near a half. Half of twelve is six, so that product is near six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Four point five times one point two is five point four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Zero point four five times twelve is also five point four.
<bookmark mark='quot'/>Fifty four divided by one point two is forty five.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four point five times one point two is fifty four point zero.
<bookmark mark='slip'/>Keeko counted only one decimal place in five hundred forty.
<bookmark mark='est'/>But four point five is near five, and one point two is near one. The product must be near five, not fifty four.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Each number has one decimal place. We must count both, two places in all, and the point goes after the five.
